topHeaders.label: Serial 1: 6 knot launch ping and recover

cells.value: Have ship’s staff bring the vessel to a cruising speed of 6 knots while maintaining a constant heading
Vessel confirmed to be cruising at 6 kts
Deploy the system at approximately 6 kts.
System is deployed
Demonstrate attenuated source txn at a depth of approximately 10 m.
Attenuated txn are successfully produced (inspect direct ping arrival on receive array)
Demonstrate towing stability at 50 m,100 m & 150 m depth (speed may be to be reduced to achieve max depth)
System towed at specific depths.
Recover the system at approximately 6 kts.
System is recovered.
Perform post recovery inspection.
System is fully stowed on winch.

System towed at specific depths.

Serial 4: Demonstration Of Test Emergency Back Up Drive - 4 kts
Have ship's staff bring the vessel to a cruising speed of 4 knots while maintaining a constant heading
Vessel confirmed to be cruising at 4 kts.
With the system still in the water, begin connecting the emergency back up drive
Back up drive connected
Manually engage the band brake actuator
Band brake engaged
Connect the emergency back up drive to the drivetrain using the appropriate chain.
Chain installed
Disconnect the main drive from the drum by disconnecting the coupler chain.
Chain coupler removed
Connect the drill to the drive, and manually disengage the band brake actuator.
Drill connected and band brake disengaged
Begin recovering the array using the drill.
Recover the array
After 10 drum turns (-30m) recovered, cease and manually re-engage the band brake actuator.
Re-engage band brake
Reconnect the drum to the main drive and disconnect the back up drive.
Drum connected
Demonstrate manual control of the levelwind and aperture with the drill
Manual control operational with drill
Recover the system.
System is recovered
Perform post recovery inspection
System is fully stowed on winch
TRAPS-9
The ATAS is to be capable of operations in littoral water as well as high sea both day and night
TRAPS-10
The ATAS and the associated equipment should be able to optimally operate in Indian waters (suited for Indian weather conditions)
TRAPS-16
For active operations, the frequency shall be less than 4 khz
TRAPS-17
For active operations, modulation – CW, HFM, and CW+HFM (wave train) and other designer specific modulation shall be suitable for Indian conditions.
TRAPS-19
For active operation, the pulse length shall be operator selectable to cater for the source and modulation.
TRAPS-21
For active operation, there shall be facility for auto detection and tracking of not less than 20 target and atleast 10 operator initiated tufts.
TRAPS-22
For active operation minimum detection range shall be 10 km with tgt strength 10 dB.
TRAPS-30
For passive operation there shall be coverage of 360 degree.
TRAPS-32
for passive operations, signal processing shall include BB, NB (LOFAR), DEMON and VERNIER (harmonics analysis)
TRAPS-42
Operator display console shall be capable of being operated from a single console.
TRAPS-44
The display should facilitate multiple windows, allowing the user to view several sets of information at one time
TRAPS-45
The display area should be approximately segregated to display data for each selected mode of operations.
TRAPS-48
Zoom controls should also be available to adjust the bearing and range scales.
TRAPS-49

Types of sonar picture displayed in the detection/ graphic area should include the following:(a) Active display – PPI (range vs bearing polar display/ B-scan (range vs bearing / A-scan (doppler vs range))(b) Passive display – A-scan (amplitude vs brg)/B-scan (doppler vs range), waterfall displays/frequency vs time (LOFAR) display(c) Tactical display – PPI Display.(d) Training aid and BIT- text and graph format
TRAPS-50

Features of the winch and handling system shall include automatic depth keeping, automatic bottom avoidance with additional capability for depth adjustment from the sonar operator console. The LRS should be able to be operated by a single operator from the control panel located in the quarterdeck. LRS should be water proof, with no light emitting from the control panel.All metal components should be protected from rust and corrosion by suitable coating.
TRAPS-52
Repeater units on displays should be available at quarterdeck, bridge and sonar console, to display the main parameter (like cable length, depth etc) while towing.
TRAPS-53

Additional features of the winch and handling System should include:(a) Towing out 'Run Out' should be impossible.(b) It should have an alternate method of recovery the Towed Equipment, in the event of primary method, in emergency.
TRAPS-57
Streaming/recovery time when towing shall be less than 30 min to 25 m depth.
TRAPS-58
ATAS should be interfaced with Gyro, Log, GPS/DGPS, COTs Radar, ASW FCS, Hull Mounted Sonar and CMS.
TRAPS-61

The ATAS should have facility for recording unprocessed data (raw data at the output of the array) and processed data (post processing at the operator console). This is primarily to facilitate reclassification of the detected tgt and review of operator tracked /detected tgts. The recorded data should be in digital format.
TRAPS-80

Built in test (BIT) for power on, online and offline system monitoring should be an integral part of system. A BIT display panel should (displayed on the operator console) should provide operator with the facility to access functional equipment performance and identify and isolated failures.
TRAPS-20
For Active operations, the range scale shall be operator selectable.
TRAPS-23
For Active operations, the own Doppler nullification shall be 0 to 20 knots.
TRAPS-24
For Active operations, there shall be Target Motion Analysis (TMA).
TRAPS-25
For active operations, there shall be facility for audio of detected targets. High fidelity and stereo.
TRAPS-26
For active operations, there shall be adaptive noise cancellation.
TRAPS-27
For active operations, there shall be adaptive beam formation.
TRAPS-28
For active operations, there shall be Shape-corrected beam forming.
TRAPS-31
For passive operations, there shall be adaptive beam formation.
TRAPS-32
For passive operations, signal processing shall include Broadband, Narrow band (LOFAR), DEMON, and VERNIER (Harmonics Analysis).
TRAPS-33
For passive operations, there shall be automatic left/right ambiguity resolution.
TRAPS-34
For passive operations, there shall be passive TMA.
TRAPS-35
For passive operations, target tracking must include at least 10 automatically and operator-initiated targets.
TRAPS-39

ATAS should have an inbuilt classifier for automatic classification of detected targets in active and passive modes. It should also have facility of an inbuilt library (of detected targets signatures). Which should updated offline and online.
TRAPS-36
For torpedo detection, there shall be coverage of 360 degrees.
TRAPS-37
For torpedo detection, tracking shall be Feature auto detection, classification, and tracking of at least 10 torpedoes, with facility for audio and visual alarm along with bearing.
TRAPS-38

For torpedo detection, with target strength of 10 dB, probability of detection of 90% and probability of false alarm 10-1, and SNR of at least -10dB at detection threshold, the detection ranges should be as follows:(i) Shallow water - ≥ 08 km(ii) Deep water - ≥ 08 km
TRAPS-39

ATAS should have an inbuilt classifier for automatic classification of detected targets in active and passive modes. It should also have facility of an inbuilt library (of detected targets signatures). Which should updated offline and online.
TRAPS-46

The detected targets and echo strength should be preferable colour coded and should be displayed along with set of information (track number, track age, track position etc). the set of information should be made available to the operator when a track is selected for analysis.
TRAPS-47

All tracks should be displayed with their latest position (range and bearing) with respect to the own ship for the last transmitted pulse. The track representation should also include successive position of the track for a maximum of eight successive pings (track history).
